text:
Maya (Finance): Heads up — Ledgerly renewal lands in 45 days and their initial renewal quote is a ~25% bump. Can we evaluate CloudSpendX as an alternative? Need: cost comparison, migration effort, and any data/export constraints. cc @Tom (procurement)

Tom (Procurement): I requested an itemized invoice from Ledgerly. Their quote breaks down as base + per-seat + data egress. CloudSpendX gave a preliminary quote that looks lower on base price but adds a per-processing fee. Need real usage to compare apples-to-apples.

Jess (SRE): From a reliability/integration POV Ledgerly already hooks into our billing pipeline. They push daily exports to S3 and we run reconciliation jobs against that. Risk switching: schema drift and replaying historical exports. I can run an export size sample and a mapping diff.

Arman (Platform): We call Ledgerly APIs for the daily reconciliation job (API key auth). CloudSpendX advertises webhook/delta sync which could eliminate a reconcile batch — might reduce reconciliation compute 10–20%. Need to see their webhook payload. Also confirm rate limits.

Leah (Legal): Note — before we engage CloudSpendX further ask for SOC2 Type II, DPA terms, data retention policy, and right-to-audit language. Also request any subprocessors list. We should not start data migration without DPAs in place.

Tom (Procurement): Negotiation levers to test: 12 vs 24 month commit (step-down pricing), migration credit, and invoice cadence. I'll ask Ledgerly for a migration credit and for CloudSpendX for a pilot discount.

Maya (Finance): Actionable ask: can someone pull last 12 months usage by sku (tokens/events/bytes exported)? If we present committed usage to Ledgerly we have leverage. Jess — can you grab the export?

Jess (SRE): I'll run the query and post a CSV to #finance-data. Quick sample of what I'll produce:

```
sku,month,tokens_processed,events,bytes_exported
billable_tokens,2025-06,1234567,12345,2345678901
realtime_events,2025-06,54321,67890,12345678
```

Jess (SRE): ETA for full 12mo export: today EOD.

Tom (Procurement): I have a draft RFP to send both vendors: pricing tiers, overage calc, egress fees, migration assistance, SLA credits, termination rights. Want eyes before I send.

Maya (Finance): +1. Target ask to test: 20% off list and 3 months free on a 12-month commit. If CloudSpendX can beat price + offer migration credit we'll pilot them on non-critical reconciliation.

vendor-bot: Ledgerly uploaded revised quote (id: 1777124000). Summary: Ledgerly 12mo list $58,000/mo (previously $46,500/mo). Notes: token tier compression, egress fee unchanged. Attachment: ledgerly_q1_renewal.pdf

Tom (Procurement): I'll open negotiations today. My initial counter: 10% off plus 6 months migration credit and tightened SLAs. If they push back, start CloudSpendX pilot and try to keep both running during migration window.

Maya (Finance): Perfect. Next steps: Jess posts the usage CSV (ETA today), Tom sends RFP to both (ETA 48h), Leah prepares DPA checklist. Reconvene after vendor replies. /remind me in 3 days to follow up.
